# mlr3changepoint

<!-- badges: start -->
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/sleepysnorlax05/mlr3changepoint/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/sleepysnorlax05/mlr3changepoint/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![codecov](https://codecov.io/github/sleepysnorlax05/mlr3changepoint/graph/badge.svg?token=AGF9QGIRKY)](https://app.codecov.io/github/sleepysnorlax05/mlr3changepoint)
[![Lifecycle: experimental](https://img.shields.io/badge/lifecycle-experimental-orange.svg)](https://lifecycle.r-lib.org/articles/stages.html#experimental)
[![pkgdown](https://github.com/sleepysnorlax05/mlr3changepoint/actions/workflows/pkgdown.yaml/badge.svg)](https://sleepysnorlax05.github.io/mlr3changepoint/)
<!-- badges: end -->

`mlr3changepoint` adds weakly supervised changepoint detection to [mlr3](https://mlr3.mlr-org.com). A changepoint or peak model needs a penalty that sets how many changes it keeps. The package learns that penalty for each sequence from labelled examples, as a function of features of the sequence. Its tasks, learners, predictions and measures work with `resample()`, `benchmark()` and tuning.

The supervision is weak. Each label covers a region of a sequence and says how many changes it holds, for example `1change` on positions 90 to 110 or `0changes` on a flat stretch. A label does not give the position of a change or a value for each point. Changepoint labels follow [penaltyLearning](https://cran.r-project.org/package=penaltyLearning), and peak labels follow [PeakError](https://cran.r-project.org/package=PeakError).

The package is developed during Google Summer of Code 2026, and its API may still change.

## Installation

```r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("sleepysnorlax05/mlr3changepoint", dependencies = TRUE)
```

`dependencies = TRUE` also installs the solvers and regressors the learners use. The MMIT and MMIF learners need the mmit package, which is not on CRAN. Its upstream sources no longer compile on macOS and Windows, so pak installs a patched copy from `sleepysnorlax05/mmit/Rpackage`.

## Learners and measures

| Learner | Regressor |
|---------|-----------|
| `changepoint.intregrcv` | L1-regularised linear interval regression (penaltyLearning) |
| `changepoint.xgboost.aft` | Gradient boosted trees with the accelerated failure time loss (xgboost) |
| `changepoint.mmit` | Maximum margin interval tree (mmit) |
| `changepoint.mmif` | Maximum margin interval forest (mmit) |

| Measure | What it scores |
|---------|----------------|
| `changepoint.label_error` | Share of labelled regions with a false positive or false negative |
| `changepoint.label_accuracy` | One minus the label error |
| `changepoint.auc` | Area under the ROC curve traced by shifting all predicted penalties |

## Example

Ten toy sequences: odd ones change mean twice and carry a `1change` label around each change, even ones are flat with a `0changes` label.

```{r example, message = FALSE}
library(mlr3)
library(mlr3changepoint)
library(data.table)

set.seed(36)
signal = vector("list", 10L)
label = vector("list", 10L)
for (i in seq_len(10L)) {
  if (i %% 2L == 1L) {
    signal[[i]] = c(rnorm(100, 18), rnorm(100, 36), rnorm(100, 9))
    label[[i]] = data.table(start = c(90, 190), end = c(110, 210), label = "1change")
  } else {
    signal[[i]] = rnorm(100, 0)
    label[[i]] = data.table(start = 1, end = 100, label = "0changes")
  }
}
task = TaskCpt$new(
  id = "toy", backend = data.table(signal = signal, label = label),
  target = "label", sequence = "signal", label_type = "changepoint"
)
```

Train the interval regression learner, predict a `log(lambda)` for each sequence, and score the label error and AUC.

```{r train}
learner = lrn("changepoint.intregrcv", Kmax = 3L, n.folds = 2L, min.observations = 2L)
learner$train(task)
prediction = learner$predict(task)
prediction$score(msrs(c("changepoint.label_error", "changepoint.auc")), task = task)
```

`autoplot()` draws each sequence with its labelled regions and dashed lines at the predicted changes.

```{r autoplot, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5, fig.alt = "Ten toy sequences with shaded labelled regions and dashed lines at the predicted changes."}
ggplot2::autoplot(prediction, task = task)
```

## Documentation

The [package website](https://sleepysnorlax05.github.io/mlr3changepoint/) starts with [Getting started](https://sleepysnorlax05.github.io/mlr3changepoint/articles/getting-started.html). It also has a chapter on each part of the package and case studies on real and simulated data. Report bugs and questions in the [issue tracker](https://github.com/sleepysnorlax05/mlr3changepoint/issues).

## Related work

- [penaltyLearning](https://cran.r-project.org/package=penaltyLearning): supervised penalty learning for changepoint detection, and the source of the labelled-region setup used here.
- [changepoint](https://cran.r-project.org/package=changepoint): classical changepoint methods. Its SegNeigh solver computes the changepoint model paths.
- [PeakSegOptimal](https://cran.r-project.org/package=PeakSegOptimal) and [PeakError](https://cran.r-project.org/package=PeakError): optimal peak models and peak label errors, used for `"peak"` labels.
- [mmit](https://github.com/aldro61/mmit): maximum margin interval trees and forests.
- [rupturesRcpp](https://cran.r-project.org/package=rupturesRcpp), [binsegRcpp](https://cran.r-project.org/package=binsegRcpp), [fpop](https://cran.r-project.org/package=fpop) and [dust](https://github.com/vrunge/dust): fast unsupervised segmentation.
